facts.text: Turtle Bay was originally a 40‑acre Dutch land grant given in 1639, later called Turtle Bay Farm.
The neighborhood takes its name from a crescent‑shaped cove that once ran from 45th to 48th Streets.
In 1917, Buster Keaton’s first silent films were shot at Comique Film Studio on East 48th Street, a warehouse later turned into a parking garage.
The Turtle Bay Association, founded in 1957, successfully opposed the widening of East 49th Street, preserving the neighborhood’s character.
The Ford Foundation Building at 42–43rd Streets east of Second Avenue is a city‑landmarked landmark, reflecting the area’s mid‑century development.
The United Nations headquarters expansion in 2000 sparked local opposition over the potential loss of Robert Moses Playground, highlighting Turtle Bay’s proximity to global diplomacy.
